back: Instructions are held in memory as binary, like data, and fetched and executed in sequence.
One memory for instructions and data and one set of buses; simple, but has the Von Neumann bottleneck.
Separate instruction and data memories with separate buses; instruction and data accessed together.
Holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched; increased during the fetch.
MAR: address of the location being accessed. MDR: data or instruction just read or about to be written.
Holds the instruction currently being decoded and executed.
Holds the results of ALU operations and the value being worked on.
Flags that record the outcome of operations, such as zero, carry, overflow and negative.

front: Roles of the ALU, CU and clock
back: ALU: arithmetic and logic. CU: fetch, decode, control signals. Clock: pulses that keep operations in step.
